headline: ENERGY FUELS ACHIEVES FULL-YEAR 2026 URANIUM GUIDANCE BY JUNE 30 — 1.6M lb U3O8 AT HISTORIC-LOW $9–$12/lb PROCESSING COST
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. (NYSE American: UUUU / TSX: EFR) announced June 11 that it expects to produce approximately 1.6 million pounds of finished uranium oxide (U3O8) by June 30 — achieving its full-year 2026 production guidance range of 1.5 to 2.5 million pounds at the halfway point of the year. Production flowed through the White Mesa Mill in Utah at a historic-low processing cost of $9–$12 per pound, well below the current $86/lb spot uranium price, confirming commercial-scale annual production rates are running before the July 2026 commencement of White Mesa's heavy rare earth circuit modifications. For uranium investors, a guidance beat at midyear confirms Energy Fuels is executing the most capital-efficient uranium production strategy among U.S. producers while simultaneously building toward the first domestic commercial-scale heavy REE separation facility.

headline: NORTHISLE DRILLS 216m AT 0.67% CuEq AT RED DOG: New High-Grade Trend Opens Below Historical Drilling at North Island BC
source_name: Investing News Network / NorthIsle Copper and Gold
snippet: NorthIsle Copper and Gold (TSXV: NCX) released June 10 results from 8,112 metres of 2026 drilling at the Red Dog deposit within the North Island Project in British Columbia — headline hole RD26-30 returned 216 metres grading 0.67% Cu Eq from 156 metres depth, including 64.1 metres at 1.10% Cu Eq from 288 metres, with four additional holes confirming broad, continuous copper-gold mineralization and establishing an emerging high-grade trend extending below the envelope targeted by most historical drilling. North Island is one of Canada's largest undeveloped copper-gold porphyry systems; with Jefferies projecting a 491,000-tonne annual copper supply deficit through 2030 and Section 232 COMEX premiums benefiting North American producers regardless of the global price cycle, results that open depth extensions at scale represent precisely the exploration upside that acquisition-minded major copper producers are currently paying premium multiples to acquire.

headline: FOMC WEEK STARTS MONDAY: 97% HOLD BUT 70% CHANCE OF DECEMBER HIKE — What Warsh's First Dot Plot Decides for Gold
snippet: GoldSilver.com's analysis ahead of Kevin Warsh's first FOMC press conference (June 16-17) frames the two-day meeting as the most consequential macro event for precious metals in 2026 — markets price a 97% probability of no rate change but simultaneously assign 70% odds of at least one hike by December, meaning the dot plot's implied path matters more than the rate decision itself. Every major institutional year-end gold forecast — Goldman Sachs $5,400, JPMorgan $6,000, Morgan Stanley $5,200, UBS $5,500 — remains intact despite gold's 25% correction from the $5,589 January peak; a Warsh framing of current 4.2% inflation as supply-shock-driven rather than demand-driven removes the rate-hike overhang that accounts for most of the gap between current spot ($4,226) and institutional targets. For self-directed junior mining investors, this binary outcome next Monday defines whether the current entry point is the cycle's best or a false bottom requiring further patience.

headline: SUN SUMMIT LAUNCHES 10,000m AT JD GOLD: 81m AT 4.80 g/t Au Near Surface, Inaugural MRE Targeted Q1 2027 in BC Toodoggone District
snippet: Sun Summit Minerals Corp. (TSXV: SMN) has commenced a fully funded 10,000-metre drill program at the JD Project in British Columbia's Toodoggone Mining District — the largest program since optioning the property in 2024, targeting an inaugural Mineral Resource Estimate in Q1 2027. Prior drilling at the Creek Zone returned 81 metres grading 4.80 g/t gold from 26 metres depth, including a 14-metre sub-interval at 19.81 g/t gold — near-surface high-grade that defines the geometry for systematic definition drilling now underway across more than 600 metres of strike. With the company fully funded and gold at $4,226/oz, Sun Summit's path to a first resource will run through the most favourable gold price backdrop in a generation without requiring dilutive equity raises during the drill program.

headline: MITHRIL SILVER: 4.01 g/t Au, 225 g/t Ag OVER 7.25m AT COPALQUIN — Updated Resource Estimate Due Late June, 25,000m Campaign 44% Complete
source_name: Mexico Mining Center / Mithril Silver and Gold
snippet: Mithril Silver and Gold Limited (TSXV: MSG / ASX: MTH) released June 10 final results from its Phase 1 El Refugio expansion at Copalquin in Durango State, Mexico — headline hole RE26-013 returned 7.25 metres grading 4.01 g/t Au and 225.1 g/t Ag (7.22 g/t AuEq) approximately 190 metres along strike from prior hole RE26-009 (9.65m at 7.00 g/t Au, 370.3 g/t Ag), confirming high-grade continuity across a growing 190-metre corridor. An updated Mineral Resource Estimate incorporating 2026 drilling is planned for late June 2026, with 11,238 metres of a 25,000-metre program now complete across the multi-target Copalquin District. At a 63.9 gold-silver ratio — the widest reading of 2026 — silver-weighted exploration companies are trading at maximum discount relative to gold, making resource-expansion catalysts like a late-June MRE update a potential re-rating trigger independent of spot price direction.

headline: LAHONTAN DISCOVERS SLAB WEST IN NEVADA: Open-All-Directions New Zone + 91m AT 0.44 g/t Au Oxide Below Calvada Resource Pit
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSXV: LG) announced June 9 results from the Santa Fe Mine Project in Nevada — geotechnical core hole CAL26-02C cut 90.8 metres grading 0.44 g/t Au Eq oxide, including 12.3 metres at 1.22 g/t, below the current Calvada resource pit shell; simultaneously, five RC holes discovered a previously unrecognized Slab West zone open in all directions. The discovery was incidental — holes drilled for mine permitting geotechnics, not exploration targeting — a pattern that historically indicates a mineralizing system larger than the current geological model. With Nevada permitting advanced and a construction decision approaching, any Slab West resource expansion increases the overall Santa Fe inventory ahead of a project valuation event where Nevada's Tier 1 jurisdiction commands a meaningful premium over comparable Latin American or African oxide heap-leach projects.

headline: MYANMAR'S CIVIL WAR IS RARE EARTH'S CHOKEPOINT: Kachin Holds 70% of China's HREE Feedstock as Military Offensives Escalate
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges examines the compounding supply-chain risk from Myanmar's civil conflict on global heavy rare earth supply — the Kachin Independence Army controls Chipwi and Pangwa township extraction areas supplying an estimated 70% of China's heavy REE feedstock including dysprosium, terbium, holmium, and yttrium, while Myanmar's military launched intensified offensives in mid-2026 under new chief Ye Win Oo to recapture these areas. The practical consequences are acute: dysprosium prices rose 105% year-to-date to approximately $930/kg and some buyers report physical access now matters more than price, with MOFCOM export licences already running 8-10 week backlogs. For investors, every Western HREE separation project — including Energy Fuels' White Mesa facility targeting Q4 2026 commercial output — represents insurance against a supply chain whose geographic concentration in an active war zone creates structural fragility that China's own export controls have already partially actualized.

headline: SILVER DEFICIT YEAR SIX: 215 Moz RECORD 2026 GAP, 762 Moz CUMULATIVE DRAWDOWN SINCE 2021 — Juniors Positioned as Physical Market Tightens
snippet: Drawing on the Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026, this analysis documents silver entering its sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit — the 2026 forecast gap of approximately 215 million ounces is the largest on record, with a cumulative 762-million-ounce drawdown from above-ground stocks since 2021. Industrial fabrication demand from AI computing infrastructure, electric vehicles, and solar remains structurally inelastic even as solar thrifting partially offsets panel-level volumes; coin and bar investment demand is forecast to rise 18% in 2026, with physical buyers treating silver simultaneously as monetary and industrial asset. At approximately $66/oz — roughly 46% below silver's January 2026 record of $121.64 and with the gold-silver ratio at its widest level of 2026 — the deficit-adjusted commodity case frames silver-weighted junior miners as offering asymmetric upside to any FOMC-driven metals recovery next week.

headline: GOLDSEEK JUNE 10: SILVER OVERSOLD BELOW $64.43 MA — BOJ Hike Fully Priced, Fed Hold Expected, Daily Gap Openings Forecast Through Month-End
snippet: Insignia Consultants' June 10 Asian metals market update on GoldSeek identifies spot silver's 50-week moving average near $64.43 as the key technical threshold — daily closes above $62.90 required to confirm a bullish trend shift — while noting that both major macro event risks for next week are effectively pre-traded: the Bank of Japan's anticipated rate hike is "fully factored in by the market" and the Federal Reserve is broadly expected to hold rates at June 16-17, removing binary shock potential from either decision. The note forecasts large daily gap openings in the Singapore session through month-end, recommending intraday rather than swing strategies for silver traders until July. For junior mining investors in silver-weighted names, the oversold technical condition combined with a market-priced macro backdrop creates a setup where the next surprise — almost certainly Warsh's dot plot tone — has asymmetric potential to trigger the short-covering recovery that extreme oversold readings historically precede.

headline: GOLD TUMBLED TO $4,161, SILVER BROKE $64 ON JUNE 10 — Week's Lows Defined by May CPI Fear Before Iran Deal Sparked $4,226 Recovery
snippet: USAGOLD's June 10 daily precious metals report captures the week's price floor for gold and silver: gold fell to $4,161 as May CPI concerns peaked (the print came in at 4.2% YoY, driven by a 23.5% energy surge from the Iran conflict), and silver broke $64 as Fed October rate-hike odds climbed to 40%. The subsequent confirmation of US-Iran peace deal progress on June 11-12 reversed most of the decline — gold recovering to $4,226 and silver to $66.53 — but the June 10 lows now establish the technical support floor that the sector defended going into FOMC week. For investors calibrating entry levels ahead of June 16-17, the fact that both metals held above key support even under simultaneous peak inflation fear and rate-hike pricing — and recovered sharply the moment one headwind partially resolved — provides evidence that the structural bid remains intact at current levels.
